newsitem.title: GERMANY: VW chief sees small 1996 profit at SEAT subsidiary.
newsitem.headline: VW chief sees small 1996 profit at SEAT subsidiary.

text.p: Volkswagen AG management board chairman Ferdinand Piech said in an interview on Thursday that troubled Spanish subsidiary SEAT would report a slight profit in 1996 but would still receive support.
Piech told the Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung in an interview that VW planned additional investments in SEAT to modernise facilities but not to boost capacity.
He said he expected SEAT to keep up its restructuring and to report positive results in the coming years without help.
"Our goal for 1997 is for profits without them having to receive help," Piech told the newspaper.
Piech also said VW's Czech unit, Skoda, would receive more than 500 million marks ($331.6 million) for investments during the year, with funds mainly targeted at finishing the Skoda Octavia vehicle.
He said further investments to boost production would follow.
